sources.title: IIIF Presentation API 3.0
sources.governing_locator: §3.2 id/width/height; §3.4 annotations/items; §3.5 motivation; §5.3 Canvas; §5.5 Annotation Page
sources.independent_observation: A Canvas is a stable page/view coordinate frame rather than an image-pixel or viewport identity. Canvas dimensions are unitless positive integers; image dimensions are pixels. Canvas IDs use HTTP(S) without fragments; selectors may identify parts. Painting and non-painting pages have different placement, and derived transcription uses supplementing. The proposal correctly separates these resources from authoring and storage. These rules support correcting the URL/pixel draft assumption, with geometry/version mapping still local.

sources.governing_locator: §3.2.4 Embedded Textual Body; §4.1 Specific Resources; §4.2.1 Fragment Selector
sources.independent_observation: TextualBody and SpecificResource/FragmentSelector provide a reusable body-target representation. Selector value is a string; type is FragmentSelector; conformsTo identifies its fragment syntax. A model does not provide editing, durable institutional storage, or every viewer feature. The proposed plain-text/rectangle subset is defensible, not independently runtime validated.

sources.title: IIIF Image API 3.0
sources.governing_locator: §1.1; §4.1 region; §4.2 size; §5.2 profile/dimensions; §5.3 Sizes; §6; §7.1 CORS; §7.3; §8 Authentication
sources.independent_observation: Request features, advertised sizes/profile, dimensions and access conditions govern image delivery. Limited/static services need not provide arbitrary crops/sizes; CORS support is recommended and authentication belongs in a separate access workflow. Rights, service availability and collection behavior cannot be inferred from an identifier. The final calls for provider-specific intake and keeps image masters remote.

sources.title: IIIF Content State API 1.0
sources.independent_observation: The API transfers a described IIIF resource/view into a compatible client. Canvas or region state needs enough Manifest context, and clients choose supported transfer mechanisms. This is distinct from maintaining a scholar’s note collection. The final’s separation of view links and annotation bundles is correct; its shorthand is not a claim that arbitrary W3C annotations can never have bodies.
